report: Jarvis V9 Brain Transplant — Legacy Dependency Audit
verdict: Your suspicion is CORRECT. V8 execution logic is still live underneath V9. There are THREE parallel control paths, not one. V9 (/v9/goal) is currently a fourth, isolated path that almost nothing routes through.

execution_graph.path_1_legacy_commander: routes/agents.py POST /agents/execute -> commander.execute_command() -> desktop_agent.* (DIRECT, bypasses orchestrator)
execution_graph.path_2_legacy_planner: routes/agents.py POST /agents/plan -> planner.create_plan() + commander.execute_plan() (open-loop, ignores verify)
execution_graph.path_4_v9_core: main.py POST /v9/goal -> OrchestratorCore.run_full_workflow() (the intended brain — but ONLY this one route reaches it)
execution_graph.path_5_bid_executor: routes/automation.py POST /automation/execute -> services.bid_executor (direct browser submit, independent of all of the above)

bypasses_orchestrator: POST /agents/desktop/* (20+ routes calling desktop_agent functions directly)

dependencies.reason: Commander still executes commands directly to desktop_agent. Spec rejection condition #1. Reachable via POST /agents/execute and from inside handle_message desktop branch. This is the primary 'V8 underneath V9' path you suspected.
Open-loop plan runner that ignores the verify field — the exact anti-pattern V9 exists to remove. Still wired to POST /agents/plan/run and /agents/auto.

Spec mandates planner.py deletion. Still called at runtime from commander.py:220, commander.py:341, and routes/agents.py:225. Cannot delete planner.py until these 3 call sites are migrated to OrchestratorCore planning.

Duplicate orchestration pipeline. Spec rejection condition: legacy execution coexisting with V9. Still reachable via POST /automation/run. Deprecation banner added previously but the ROUTE still calls it live.

A THIRD pipeline, separate from both automation_engine and OrchestratorCore. Reachable via POST /orchestrator/start. Note: agents/orchestrator.py also hosts STATE (the SSE feed) which IS still needed — so the file cannot be deleted wholesale, only start_pipeline removed.

Real browser submit path reachable via /automation/execute independent of orchestrator. Not legacy per se (it's the actual working submit), but it bypasses the V9 control loop, so an autonomous run and a manual queue execution can both drive the browser with no shared coordination. Must be made a tool the ExecutorAgent calls, not a parallel entrypoint.

Direct desktop_agent function exposure (click, type, open_app, etc.). These are useful as manual/debug tools and as the ExecutorAgent's action primitives. Not a blocker IF the autonomous path stops using them as its control flow — but they must not remain an alternative *workflow* entry. Keep as primitives, remove any workflow logic.
The SSE event bus. Required infrastructure, used by V9 core too. Keep. Do NOT delete agents/orchestrator.py wholesale — extract/keep STATE.
used_by: everything that emits to the live feed, including orchestrator_core.py

dependencies.reason: The NEW V9 executor currently falls back to commander.execute_command for desktop actions. This means even the V9 path re-enters legacy commander execution. Must be rewired to call desktop_agent primitives directly, or commander.execute_command can never be removed.

migration_blockers: BLOCKER: 3 live call sites of planner.create_plan must be migrated before planner.py can be deleted.
BLOCKER: POST /automation/run still calls run_auto_mode — route must be repointed to OrchestratorCore before automation_engine deletion.
BLOCKER: commander.execute_command/execute_plan still wired to /agents/execute, /agents/plan/run, /agents/auto — these routes must be repointed or removed.
HIGH: V9 executor itself calls commander.execute_command as a fallback — self-defeating; rewire to desktop_agent primitives.
HIGH: POST /orchestrator/start (legacy pipeline) and POST /automation/run (engine) are two more pipelines that must be collapsed into OrchestratorCore.
CONSTRAINT: agents/orchestrator.py cannot be deleted — it hosts STATE (SSE). Extract STATE or keep the file and remove only start_pipeline.

challenges_to_spec.audit_finding: AGREE it should go, but it has 3 live callers. Deleting it now breaks /agents/plan, /agents/auto, and commander's plan branch immediately. Must migrate callers FIRST. Sequencing challenge, not a disagreement.
challenges_to_spec.recommendation: Migrate the 3 call sites to OrchestratorCore.PLANNING, THEN delete planner.py.

challenges_to_spec.audit_finding: AGREE, but POST /automation/run is still live-wired to it and the frontend Auto Mode page may call it. Deleting the file without repointing the route is a guaranteed 500 error on that page.

challenges_to_spec.spec_says: Delete any routes bypassing orchestrator (implies the /agents/desktop/* routes)
challenges_to_spec.audit_finding: PARTIAL DISAGREE. The 20+ desktop primitive routes should NOT all be deleted — the ExecutorAgent needs those exact functions as its action primitives, and they're valuable as manual/debug controls. What must be removed is their use as an alternative *workflow/control* path, not the primitives themselves.
challenges_to_spec.recommendation: Keep desktop_agent primitives + their thin routes; remove only workflow-bearing routes (execute_command, execute_plan, run_auto_mode, start_pipeline).

challenges_to_spec.audit_finding: AGREE and FLAG: current perception_agent.py is Stage-1 text-only (OCR/vision text). Meeting this spec requires real Playwright DOM extraction (role/text/bbox/clickable). This is genuine new work, not a wiring change, and it is the single highest-effort item in the transplant.
challenges_to_spec.recommendation: Treat structured browser perception as the critical-path deliverable, not a side task.

challenges_to_spec.audit_finding: DISAGREE. It hosts STATE (the SSE event bus) that V9 itself depends on. Deleting it breaks the live feed everywhere.
challenges_to_spec.recommendation: Keep the file or relocate STATE into core/; never delete wholesale.

summary.headline: V9 exists but is an island. Four legacy/parallel execution paths still drive desktop and browser without going through OrchestratorCore. The brain transplant cannot be called done until /agents/execute, /agents/plan*, /automation/run, /orchestrator/start are repointed or removed, planner.py's 3 callers are migrated, and the V9 executor stops falling back into commander.execute_command.

next_step: AWAITING APPROVAL. No code will be written until you approve this report and the proposed sequencing (migrate callers -> repoint routes -> delete legacy -> then structured perception).
